recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If future work wants to revisit bodySite extension canonical naming, handle it as an extension-pack or compatibility policy question rather than as a core BodySite resource rename fix.
issue_request: FHIR-13396 was a Published/Persuasive OO change request from STU3 to rename BodySite to BodyStructure because the resource needed to represent things such as tumors rather than only anatomical locations, and to align affected body-site extensions.
initial_application: Historical commit 386071a8e535114ff8df5ae7611b966cf354b3cb renamed the active resource entry, folder, examples, resource pages, extension references, and related narrative from BodySite/bodysite/body-site-instance to BodyStructure/bodystructure/body-structure. Commit ca3c7d832757cc1f958071ec5788462aea3c0cb0 added BodySite to the removed-resource list, and cc0dad0855c57bc2eee75736c3e72867c6635930 preapplied the linked BodyStructure morphology/location work from FHIR-13394.
additional_context: Current source/fhir.ini lists bodystructure=BodyStructure as an active resource and retains BodySite only in removed-resource, comment, and R2-rename compatibility contexts. The authoritative BodyStructure definition, examples, and narrative use BodyStructure. Remaining bodySite/body-site strings checked during reconciliation are anatomical-site element/search-parameter/value-set names, legacy compatibility metadata, or extension-pack definitions whose current value targets BodyStructure rather than a BodySite resource. The referenced Zulip thread supports the rename rationale, and no direct Confluence references to FHIR-13396 were found.
reconciliation: No source files were changed because the current built core source already implements the requested BodySite-to-BodyStructure rename and the checked extension evidence does not show a remaining core source defect.

related_jiras.note: The linked BodySite.kind issue refined the renamed BodyStructure model into separate location/morphology semantics and explains why later source may not literally match the old BodySite wording.
